To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the contention resolution problem can be solved in O(log n) time with constant expected delay, even when the number of users is unbounded, and the generation rate is 1/10 or less.
contention resolution is possible for a Poisson arrival process with rate up to 0.37, and for a Bernoulli arrival process with rate less than 1/e.

(a) contention resolution with a constant expected average delay is achievable in a model with an infinite number of asynchronous users and (b) contention resolution with constant expected message delay is achievable in models with a finite number of asynchronous and/or synchronized users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How much does the expected delay of a message depend on the number of users and on the distribution of the message arrivals?
contention resolution in multiple-access channels.
the following problem: How can we design contention resolution protocols that have a constant expected delay for a large range of message arrival processes?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for any fixed number of users, the expected delay of a message is O( (1 + log n)/n) when messages are Bernoulli distributed with generation rate up/10, and is O(1/n) when messages are Poisson distributed with generation rate smaller than e.
for any given message, the delay in our contention resolution protocols is constant with high probability, even if the channel is saturated.
we have given a protocol with O(1) expected delay in the case of a Bernoulli model with generation rate smaller than e, or a Poisson model with rate smaller than 2e.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed the following two protocols: (1) a contention resolution protocol with constant expected delay in a model in which users have a Bernoulli message generation rate of 1/e and are synchronized; (2) a contention resolution algorithm with expected delay of O(log n) in a model in where users have a Bernollli message generation rate smaller than about 1/9.

we give contention resolution protocols for a model with a finite number of users, for a model with an infinite number of synchronized users and for a model with synchronized users with an infinite number, and in all cases we achieve a constant expected delay for a constant generation rate.
we have developed a framework for the design of contention resolution protocols with small expected delay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contention resolution protocols can have constant expected delay even in the worst-case.
contention resolution can be done with expected constant delay, even when messages are generated at high rates.
contention resolution is feasible even in very general models, and that it is possible to design protocols that have constant expected delay for a large class of message generation distributions.
